question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: How is your currant brand strategy workinng?
option_2: How is your current brrand strategy working?
option_3: How is your current brand stretagy working?
option_4: How is your current brand strategy working?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. How is your current brand strategy working?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 4 is spelt correctly — "current" (present, of the present time), "brand", "strategy" and "working".

◦ Correct: How is your current brand strategy working?

• Spelling keys: CUR + RENT, STRA + TE + GY, WORK + ING (single "n").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells two words — "currant" (a small dried grape, a fruit) instead of "current", and "workinng" instead of "working".

• Option 2 misspells "brand" as "brrand" (double "r").

• Option 3 misspells "strategy" as "stretagy".

NOTE

• Beware of the homophone pair current (adjective — present/prevailing; noun — flow of water or electricity) and currant (a dried grape or a small berry). SSC frequently tests such confusable pairs: stationary/stationery, principal/principle, complement/compliment.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

After suffering so many losses, the company is about to go ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bankrupt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bankrupt" means declared legally unable to pay one's debts; financially ruined. The clue "after suffering so many losses" and "the company" clearly points to financial collapse. (दिवालिया)

◦ Correct: After suffering so many losses, the company is about to go bankrupt.

• "Go bankrupt" is a fixed collocation used for businesses that fail financially.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "silent" (making no sound) does not fit a company suffering losses.

• Option 3 "cynical" (believing that people act only out of self-interest) describes an attitude, not a financial state.

• Option 4 "awry" (wrong, off course) is used as "go awry" but refers to plans going wrong, not to financial ruin caused by losses.

NOTE

• Useful "go + adjective" collocations: go bankrupt, go bald, go mad, go sour, go stale, go missing, go public. Related words: bankruptcy (noun), insolvent (synonym), liquidation, solvent (antonym).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Fit as a fiddle
option_1: In a very good physical condition
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In a very good physical condition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(as) fit as a fiddle" means in very good health; perfectly fit physically. (पूरी तरह स्वस्थ / चुस्त-दुरुस्त)

◦ Example: At eighty, my grandfather is still as fit as a fiddle.

• Here "fit" carries its older sense of "in fine condition", and the "fiddle" (violin) is imagined as being finely tuned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To be in love" would be expressed by idioms like "head over heels" or "smitten".

• Option 3 "To drink alcohol regularly" corresponds to "hit the bottle".

• Option 4 "To be firm" corresponds to "put one's foot down" or "stand one's ground".

NOTE

• Other health-related idioms: "in the pink (of health)", "alive and kicking", "hale and hearty", "back on one's feet" (recovered after illness), "under the weather" (slightly unwell — the opposite).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Shapes that are impossible to make of machining can be printed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to make of machining.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When we name the means, method or process by which something is done, the correct preposition is "by", not "of". So the segment must be "to make by machining".

◦ Correct: Shapes that are impossible to make by machining can be printed.

• "By + noun/gerund" = the method used: made by hand, travel by bus, killed by poison, produced by machining.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "Shapes that are impossible" is correct — "impossible" is properly followed by the to-infinitive.

• Segment 3 "can be printed." is a correct passive form (modal + be + V3), fitting the context of 3-D printing.

• Since a definite error exists in segment 4, "No error" (Option 2) cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Distinguish: "made of" (the material that is still visible — a table made of wood), "made from" (the material that is transformed — wine made from grapes), "made by" (the agent or the process — a chair made by a carpenter / made by machining), "made with" (the ingredients or tools used).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

The government appears (to be at war with it's own people.)
option_1: to be on war with it's own people
option_2: to be at war against it's own people
option_4: to be at war with its own people
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to be at war with its own people.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two things must be fixed in the bracketed part:

◦ The possessive adjective is "its" (belonging to it). "It's" is the short form of "it is / it has" and is wrong here.

◦ The standard collocation is "at war with" (to be engaged in conflict with someone), not "on war with".

• Correct: The government appears to be at war with its own people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the wrong preposition "on war" and also keeps the wrong "it's".

• Option 2 keeps the wrong "it's"; "at war against" is also unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed sentence contains the error "it's".

NOTE

• Remember: its = possessive (The dog wagged its tail); it's = it is / it has (It's raining). Possessive pronouns — its, hers, ours, yours, theirs — never take an apostrophe. Related collocations: at war with, at peace with, at odds with, at loggerheads with.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Mad
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sound.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mad" means mentally ill, insane or irrational. Its antonym is "sound", which means healthy, sane and in good condition — as in the phrase "of sound mind". (पागल का विलोम — स्वस्थ चित्त / समझदार)

◦ Example: The court held that the old man was of sound mind when he wrote the will.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Indisposition" means a slight illness or an unwillingness — it is not the opposite of madness.

• Option 3 "Distemper" means a disease of animals (or a kind of paint), and in older usage a disordered state of mind — closer to a synonym.

• Option 4 "Dense" means thick or (informally) stupid — again not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of mad: insane, lunatic, deranged, demented, crazy. Antonyms: sane, sound, rational, lucid, sensible. "Mad" can also mean "very angry" (mad at someone) or "very enthusiastic" (mad about cricket).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time marker "yesterday" requires the simple past tense. The verb "shine" is irregular: shine – shone – shone. So the past form is "shone".

◦ Correct: Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun shone.

• "The sun shone" is the natural collocation for sunlight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "shown" is the past participle of "show" (show – showed – shown), not of "shine", and it also needs an auxiliary (has shown).

• Options 1 "flamed" and 4 "burned" are grammatically past forms but do not collocate naturally with "the sun" in this weather contrast.

NOTE

• Note the two past forms of "shine": shone (gave out light — the sun shone) and shined (polished — he shined his shoes). Other irregular verbs often tested: fly–flew–flown, lie–lay–lain, lay–laid–laid, rise–rose–risen.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The Gryffindors trooped back up / to the castle, none of them talking; / it have been another long day.
option_3: it have been another long day.
option_4: to the castle, none of them talking;
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. it have been another long day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "it" is third person singular, so it can never take "have". Moreover, the narration is in the past ("trooped"), so the past perfect "had been" is required for the earlier state.

◦ Correct: The Gryffindors trooped back up to the castle, none of them talking; it had been another long day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "The Gryffindors trooped back up" is correct — "trooped" is the simple past of "troop" (to move in a group).

• Segment "to the castle, none of them talking;" is a correct absolute (nominative absolute) phrase: noun/pronoun + participle.

• As a clear error exists, "No error" cannot be the answer.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement with "it/he/she" takes has (present) and the past perfect uses had + V3 for the earlier of two past actions. Compare: "It has been a long day" (present perfect) / "It had been a long day" (past perfect).

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Valet
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Butler.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "valet" is a male personal attendant/servant who looks after his employer's clothes and personal needs; a "butler" is likewise a male domestic servant in charge of a household. The two are the closest in meaning among the options. (निजी सेवक / परिचारक)

◦ Example: The valet laid out his master's evening clothes.

• A valet also means a hotel attendant who parks guests' cars (valet parking).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Carrier" means one who carries goods, or a company that transports things.

• Option 2 "Carrousel" (carousel) is a merry-go-round, or the moving belt at an airport that delivers luggage.

• Option 3 "Kingpin" means the most important person in an organisation — the opposite of a servant.

NOTE

• Household staff vocabulary often asked in SSC exams: butler (chief male servant), valet (personal male attendant), maid (female domestic servant), chauffeur (a paid car driver), steward (one who manages property or serves on a ship/plane).

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

I was (disappointed) to see the lack of coverage afforded to this event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Encouraged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Disappointed" means saddened or let down because one's hopes were not fulfilled. Its antonym here is "encouraged", meaning filled with hope, confidence and enthusiasm. (निराश का विलोम — प्रोत्साहित)

◦ Example: I was encouraged to see how much coverage the event finally received.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dizzy" (giddy, light-headed) is unrelated to the emotion of disappointment.

• Option 2 "Humiliated" (made to feel ashamed) is a negative emotion, not an antonym.

• Option 4 "Gloomy" (sad, dejected) is a near synonym of disappointed.

NOTE

• Synonyms of disappointed: disheartened, dejected, let down, dissatisfied, crestfallen. Antonyms: encouraged, pleased, satisfied, delighted, heartened. Related word: "afforded" here means "given/provided".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Paradise
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bliss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paradise" means heaven; a place or state of perfect happiness and delight. Its closest synonym among the options is "bliss", which means perfect happiness or great joy. (स्वर्ग / परम आनंद)

◦ Example: The quiet hill station was sheer paradise/bliss after the noise of the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Trivial" means unimportant or of little value.

• Option 3 "Display" means to show or exhibit something.

• Option 4 "Ghost" means the spirit of a dead person — none of these carries the sense of supreme happiness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of paradise: heaven, Eden, utopia, bliss, nirvana. Antonyms: hell, hades, inferno, purgatory. Note the related adjective "blissful" and the idiom "a fool's paradise" (a state of false happiness based on illusions).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

He suggested (there was collusions through objectors, due to similarities) in some letters sent to the council.
option_1: there was collusions from the objector, due to similarities
option_2: there was collusion between objectors, due to similarities
option_4: their was collusion by the objectors, due to similarities
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. there was collusion between objectors, due to similarities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Collusion" (secret cooperation for a dishonest purpose) is an uncountable noun, so it must be singular after "there was" — "there was collusion", never "there was collusions". (मिलीभगत / साँठगाँठ)

• Secret cooperation always takes place "between/among" the parties involved, so "collusion between objectors" is the correct phrase, not "collusion through objectors".

◦ Correct: He suggested there was collusion between objectors, due to similarities in some letters sent to the council.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the ungrammatical plural "collusions" and illogically pairs a plural idea with the singular "the objector".

• Option 3 is wrong because the printed segment has two errors (plural "collusions" and the preposition "through").

• Option 4 wrongly uses "their" (possessive) in place of "there" (the introductory/existential word).

NOTE

• Common uncountable nouns tested by SSC: information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment, machinery, evidence, collusion, progress. They take singular verbs and no "-s". Also revise the trio their (possessive) / there (place or existential) / they're (they are).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A woman with brown hair
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Brunette.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "brunette" is a woman or girl with brown or dark hair. (भूरे बालों वाली महिला)

◦ Example: The tall brunette in the front row answered every question.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Blonde" is the opposite — a woman with fair or golden hair.

• Option 1 "Blunt" means not sharp, or (of speech) very direct and frank.

• Option 4 "Bumble" means to move or speak in a clumsy, confused way.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes on appearance: redhead (a person with red hair), brunette (brown-haired woman), blonde/blond (fair-haired), albino (a person born without normal pigmentation), bald (having no hair).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The story of human evolution ______ a moving target in recent years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in recent years" signals an action or state that began in the past and continues into the present, which requires the present perfect tense.

• The subject is "The story of human evolution" — the head noun is the singular "story" ("of human evolution" is only a modifying phrase), so the singular auxiliary "has" is needed.

◦ Correct: The story of human evolution has been a moving target in recent years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had being" is ungrammatical — after "had" we need the past participle "been", not "being".

• Option 3 "have been" wrongly uses the plural auxiliary with the singular subject "story".

• Option 4 "did has" is doubly wrong — "did" is already a past auxiliary and must be followed by the base form.

NOTE

• Rule of proximity trap: the verb agrees with the head noun, not with the noun nearest to it. "The box of chocolates is on the table", "The quality of the mangoes was poor". Present perfect markers: since, for, recently, in recent years, so far, already, just, yet.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

That new budget bill was (totally useless) before it hit the Senate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a dead duck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a dead duck" means something that is doomed to fail; a plan or proposal that is already useless and has no chance of success. It fits "totally useless" perfectly. (जो पहले ही विफल हो चुका हो / बेकार)

◦ Example: Without the ruling party's support, the bill was a dead duck.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cry wolf" means to raise a false alarm repeatedly, so that people stop believing you.

• Option 3 "cold feet" (to get cold feet) means to lose one's nerve at the last moment.

• Option 4 "add fuel to the fire" means to make a bad situation worse.

NOTE

• Other idioms of failure: "fall flat", "come to nothing", "go up in smoke", "a lost cause", "dead in the water". Note that "hit the Senate" here simply means "reached the Senate for discussion".

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ARGUMENT.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "ARGUMENT" is spelt correctly. It means a disagreement or a reason given in support of an idea. (तर्क / बहस)

• Spelling key: ARGUE loses its final "e" before "-ment" — ARGU + MENT (no "e" after "u").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "CALANDER" is misspelt; the correct spelling is "CALENDAR" (a chart of the days of the year).

• Option 2 "SPLATER" is misspelt; the correct spelling is "SPLATTER" (to splash liquid noisily — double "t").

• Option 3 "ASSASINATION" is misspelt; the correct spelling is "ASSASSINATION" (double "s" twice — AS + SAS + SIN + ATION).

NOTE

• Words that drop the final "e" before "-ment": argue → argument, judge → judgment (British also judgement), true → truly, due → duly. Words retaining "e": manage → management, achieve → achievement.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

My grandmother taught me how to sew my own clothes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "taught me" is already correct:

◦ "taught" is the correct past tense (teach – taught – taught), matching the past narration.

◦ "me" is the objective form of "I" and is the correct indirect object of the verb "taught".

• Correct as printed: My grandmother taught me how to sew my own clothes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "teach mine" is wrong on two counts — the tense (present "teach") and the possessive pronoun "mine" in place of an object.

• Option 2 "taught myself" changes the meaning entirely (it would mean the grandmother taught herself) and misuses the reflexive pronoun, since the subject and object are different people.

• Option 4 "taught I" wrongly uses the subject pronoun "I" where the object form "me" is needed.

NOTE

• Subject pronouns: I, we, he, she, they, who. Object pronouns: me, us, him, her, them, whom. Reflexive pronouns (myself, herself) are used only when the subject and the object are the same person: "I taught myself to swim".

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The act of destroying or damaging something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sabotage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sabotage" means the deliberate act of destroying, damaging or obstructing something, especially machinery, property or a plan. (तोड़फोड़ / विध्वंस)

◦ Example: The factory fire was found to be an act of sabotage by a rival firm.

• It works both as a noun (an act of destruction) and as a verb (to sabotage a plan).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vengeance" and Option 4 "Revenge" both mean harm done in return for an injury — they describe a motive of retaliation, not the act of destruction itself.

• Option 2 "Avenge" is a verb meaning to take revenge on behalf of someone, so it cannot substitute a noun phrase describing an act of destruction.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: vandalism (wilful destruction of public property), arson (deliberately setting fire to property), demolition (pulling down a structure), saboteur (a person who commits sabotage).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

I am sorry that I was unable to see ______ of you over the summer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "See more of somebody" is a fixed English expression meaning to meet or spend time with someone more often. The speaker regrets not having met the listener more frequently.

◦ Correct: I am sorry that I was unable to see more of you over the summer.

• Similar structures: "We must see more of each other", "We saw very little of him last year".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "many of you" would refer to a number of people, but "you" here is a single addressee and the sense required is frequency, not number.

• Option 3 "much of you" is unidiomatic in this construction of meeting someone.

• Option 4 "many more of you" again wrongly counts people instead of expressing frequency of meeting.

NOTE

• Contrast the quantifiers: many/few with countable nouns (many books), much/little with uncountable nouns (much water). In the idiom "see more/less of someone", "more" and "less" refer to the amount of time spent together.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Our passage across the Arabian Sea/ was smooth as the most timid of/ navigators could desire.
option_2: Our passage across the Arabian Sea
option_3: was smooth as the most timid of
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was smooth as the most timid of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A comparison of equality in English requires the pair "as ... as". The sentence compares the smoothness of the passage with what a timid navigator could wish for, so the first "as" is missing.

◦ Correct: Our passage across the Arabian Sea was as smooth as the most timid of navigators could desire.

• Structure: as + adjective/adverb (positive degree) + as.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "Our passage across the Arabian Sea" is correct — "across" is the right preposition for movement from one side to the other.

• Segment "navigators could desire." is correct; "the most timid of navigators" means "even the most timid navigator".

• Because a definite error exists, "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Comparison structures: equality — as ... as (as tall as); negative equality — not so/as ... as; comparative — -er/more ... than; superlative — the ... -est / the most. Note that only the positive degree of the adjective appears between "as ... as".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod (1) ______ “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) ______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas, obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) ______ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. wrote.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states a completed historical fact with a definite past time marker — "In 700 BCE". A finished action at a stated past time requires the simple past tense, so "wrote" is correct.

◦ Correct: In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod wrote "Theogony" and "Work and Days".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had written" (past perfect) needs a second, later past action to relate to; none is given here.

• Option 2 "will write" is future tense and contradicts "In 700 BCE".

• Option 4 "writes" is simple present and cannot be used with a finished past date.

NOTE

• Golden rule: a definite past time expression (yesterday, last year, in 1947, in 700 BCE) always takes the simple past, never the present perfect. Verb forms: write – wrote – written.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod (1) ______ “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) ______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas, obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) ______ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To describe a quality or attribute that a person possesses, English uses the preposition "of" — "a man of courage", "a woman of great wisdom", "a Titan of enormous strength".

◦ Correct: Atlas was a Titan of enormous strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "from" indicates origin or source (a scholar from Greece).

• Option 2 "in" indicates place or state (a Titan in chains).

• Option 4 "at" indicates a point of place or time (at the gate, at noon) — none of them expresses an inherent quality.

NOTE

• "Of" is used for possession or description: a man of letters (a learned person), a person of means (rich), a matter of importance, a girl of ten. Learn such prepositional phrases as fixed units.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod (1) ______ “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) ______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas, obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) ______ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. challenged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The very next sentence says the Titans were defeated by the god Zeus and banished to Tartarus. That is possible only if they had fought against / opposed the Olympian gods. "Challenged" means to confront, defy or fight against. (चुनौती देना)

◦ Correct: He along with other titans challenged the gods of Mount Olympus.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "collaborated" means to work together with someone — the exact opposite of the conflict described.

• Option 2 "claimed" means to assert a right to something; it also needs a different object.

• Option 4 "corroborated" means to confirm or support a statement with evidence, which makes no sense with "the gods".

NOTE

• Context clue technique: read the sentences after the blank. Words such as "defeated", "banished" and "retribution" all signal conflict, so only a word of opposition can fit. Synonyms of challenge: defy, confront, dispute, contest.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod (1) ______ “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) ______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas, obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) ______ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. however.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence sets up a contrast: the other Titans were banished to Tartarus, but Atlas received a different punishment — carrying the earth and the sky. The contrast connector "however" fits between the subject and the verb and is set off in the sentence.

◦ Correct: While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus ..., Atlas however was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "despite" is a preposition and must be followed by a noun or gerund (despite the defeat), not by a verb phrase.

• Option 3 "in fact" is used to add emphasis or a confirming detail, not to mark contrast between two different fates.

• Option 4 "unlike" is also a preposition needing a noun after it (unlike the other Titans).

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: however, nevertheless, nonetheless, on the contrary, on the other hand (used with a full clause); despite / in spite of (followed by a noun or -ing form); although / though / while (followed by a clause).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

In 700 BCE Greek poet Hesiod (1) ______ “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) ______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas, obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) ______ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. globe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The very next sentence supplies the answer: "Because of his association with the globe, maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas." So the stooped figure is shown carrying the globe on his shoulders. (गोला / पृथ्वी का गोलक)

◦ Correct: ... he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the globe on his shoulders.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "universe" and Option 4 "heavens" are too vast and are not repeated later in the passage.

• Option 3 "seas" has no connection with the image of a figure bearing a round object on his shoulders.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, the correct word is very often repeated or paraphrased nearby — always scan the following sentence. Interesting fact: a book of maps is called an "atlas" precisely because early map collections carried a picture of Atlas bearing the globe.

question: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) now has in excess of 472 million accounts. Which state has topped this list (as on October 12, 2022)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As on 12 October 2022, Uttar Pradesh topped the list of states with the highest number of accounts opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), followed by Bihar and West Bengal. (उत्तर प्रदेश)

• Being the most populous state, UP naturally accounts for the largest share of the 47.2 crore (472 million) Jan-Dhan accounts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a National Mission on Financial Inclusion, under the Ministry of Finance.

• It offers a zero-balance (no minimum balance) savings account, a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover, overdraft facility and access to pension and insurance schemes.

• PMJDY accounts form the backbone of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and the JAM trinity — Jan-Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile.

NOTE

• PMJDY entered the Guinness World Records for the most bank accounts opened in one week (2014). Nearly 56% of Jan-Dhan account holders are women and about 67% of accounts are in rural and semi-urban areas.

question: According to census 2011, which of the following is NOT included in top ten most populous countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Canada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Canada is not among the world's ten most populous countries. Despite being the second largest country in the world by area, Canada has a small population (about 3.4 crore at that time) because much of its land is cold and sparsely settled. (कनाडा)

• Around the time of the 2011 Census, the ten most populous countries were China, India, USA, Indonesia, Brazil, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Russia and Japan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pakistan, Nigeria and Japan all featured in that top-ten list, so they cannot be the answer.

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence; India's population was recorded as 121.08 crore.

• Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future", and it introduced the National Population Register (NPR).

NOTE

• Census 2011 data: Sex ratio 943, literacy rate 74.04%, density 382 persons per sq km. Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest literacy — Bihar.

question: One of the major hubs of information technology is the Silicon valley which is situated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is California.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Silicon Valley is located in the southern part of the San Francisco Bay Area in the US state of California. It is the world's leading hub of information technology, semiconductors and start-ups. (कैलिफ़ोर्निया)

• The name comes from "silicon", the semiconductor material used to make computer chips, and the valley (Santa Clara Valley) where the early chip companies were founded.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Global technology giants headquartered there include Apple, Google (Alphabet), Meta (Facebook), Intel, Cisco, Adobe, Oracle and Nvidia.

• Stanford University in the region played a key role in nurturing the Valley's start-up culture.

NOTE

• India's own "Silicon Valley of India" is Bengaluru (Bangalore), Karnataka. Other Indian IT hubs: Hyderabad (Cyberabad/HITEC City), Pune, Chennai, Noida and Gurugram.

question: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Speaker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) is the "Speaker", elected by the members of the House from among themselves. (लोकसभा अध्यक्ष)

• The Speaker maintains order in the House, decides points of order, certifies a Money Bill (Article 110) and presides over joint sittings of Parliament (Article 108).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The office of the Speaker is provided for in Article 93 of the Constitution.

• India's first Speaker of the Lok Sabha was G. V. Mavalankar, known as the "Father of the Lok Sabha".

• The Speaker votes only in the case of a tie — a casting vote.

NOTE

• The Rajya Sabha is presided over by the Chairman, who is the Vice-President of India (Article 89), assisted by a Deputy Chairman. The Lok Sabha also has a Deputy Speaker (Article 93) who presides in the Speaker's absence.

question: Which among the following is the coldest of the atmospheric layers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mesosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "mesosphere" is the coldest layer of the Earth's atmosphere. Temperature falls with height in this layer and reaches about -90°C to -100°C at its upper boundary, the mesopause. (मध्यमंडल — सबसे ठंडी परत)

• It extends roughly from 50 km to 80–85 km above the Earth's surface.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Troposphere (0–about 18 km at the equator) — the lowest layer where all weather phenomena occur; temperature falls with height.

• Stratosphere (about 18–50 km) — contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays; ideal for jet aircraft flight.

• Thermosphere (above 80 km) — temperature rises sharply; contains the ionosphere, which reflects radio waves back to the Earth.

• Exosphere — the outermost layer, merging into space.

NOTE

• Meteors burn up in the mesosphere, which is why we see "shooting stars" there. The rare, high-altitude noctilucent clouds also form in this layer.

question: Which among the following Acts discarded the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level and allowed for the emergence of popularly elected provincial legislatures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act, 1935.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced "provincial autonomy", under which provinces became autonomous units administered by popularly elected ministers responsible to the provincial legislatures. (1935 का भारत शासन अधिनियम — प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता)

• Ironically, it introduced dyarchy at the Centre instead (though this was never implemented).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dyarchy (double government) in the provinces was first introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms), which divided provincial subjects into "transferred" (under Indian ministers) and "reserved" (under the Governor).

• The 1935 Act also provided for an All-India Federation, a Federal Court (1937) and the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India, and it extended the franchise to about 10% of the population.

• It divided powers into three lists — Federal, Provincial and Concurrent — a scheme our Constitution later adopted.

NOTE

• Other Acts: Pitt's India Act, 1784 set up the Board of Control (dual government by Company and Crown); the Charter Act, 1793 renewed the Company's trade monopoly for 20 years; the Charter Act, 1813 ended the Company's Indian trade monopoly.

question: According to 2011 Census, which among the following state has the highest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 2011, Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state of India, with a population of about 19.98 crore (199.8 million), i.e., roughly 16.5% of India's total population. (उत्तर प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या)

• The next most populous states are Maharashtra (11.24 crore), Bihar (10.41 crore) and West Bengal (9.13 crore).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Least populous state — Sikkim (about 6.1 lakh); least populous Union Territory — Lakshadweep.

• Most densely populated state — Bihar (1,106 persons per sq km); least dense — Arunachal Pradesh (17).

• Largest state by area — Rajasthan; smallest by area — Goa.

NOTE

• Census 2011 highlights: total population 121.08 crore; decadal growth 17.7%; sex ratio 943 females per 1,000 males (highest in Kerala – 1,084, lowest in Haryana – 879); child sex ratio 919.

question: Lovlina Borgohain is associated with which sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Boxing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lovlina Borgohain, from Assam, is an Indian boxer. She won a bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) in the women's welterweight (69 kg) category. (लवलीना बोरगोहेन — मुक्केबाज़ी)

• She later won gold at the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 in New Delhi (75 kg) and at the Asian Games 2022 (Hangzhou).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She was honoured with the Arjuna Award (2020) and the Padma Shri (2021).

• Only three Indian boxers have won Olympic medals — Vijender Singh (2008), Mary Kom (2012) and Lovlina Borgohain (2021).

NOTE

• Boxing terms: knockout (KO), jab, hook, uppercut, bout, round, southpaw. The sport is governed internationally by the International Boxing Association (IBA) and in India by the Boxing Federation of India (BFI).

question: Who among the following wrote the biography of Jahangir known as Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mutamid Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri" is a biography/history of the Mughal emperor Jahangir, written in Persian by Mutamid Khan, who was an officer and chronicler in Jahangir's court. (मुतामिद ख़ान)

• The work is in three volumes and covers the reigns of Babur and Humayun, of Akbar, and then Jahangir's own reign in detail.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jahangir himself wrote his memoirs, the "Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri" (Jahangirnama), in Persian.

• Abul Fazl wrote the "Akbarnama" and the "Ain-i-Akbari" during Akbar's reign.

• Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan was one of Akbar's navratnas, famous for his Hindi couplets (dohas) and for translating the Baburnama into Persian.

NOTE

• Important Mughal chronicles: Baburnama (Babur, in Turkish), Humayunnama (Gulbadan Begum), Akbarnama (Abul Fazl), Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (Jahangir), Padshahnama (Abdul Hamid Lahori, on Shah Jahan) and Alamgirnama (Mirza Muhammad Kazim, on Aurangzeb).

question: Which of the following dances is a popular folk dance of Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lavani" is the famous folk dance and song form of Maharashtra, traditionally performed by women wearing a nine-yard saree (nauvari) to the beat of the dholki drum. (लावणी — महाराष्ट्र)

• The word is believed to come from "lavanya", meaning beauty. It is a major part of Marathi Tamasha folk theatre.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Bihu" is the folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bihu festival.

• Option 3 "Jhumar (Jhumur)" is associated with Punjab/Haryana and also with the tribal belt of Jharkhand and West Bengal.

• Option 4 "Giddha" is a lively folk dance of the women of Punjab.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Maharashtra: Tamasha, Powada, Dindi, Kala and Koli (the fishermen's dance). Some state folk dances: Gujarat — Garba/Dandiya; Rajasthan — Ghoomar/Kalbelia; Uttar Pradesh — Raslila/Charkula; Kerala — Kaikottikali/Theyyam.

question: ______ was founded by Dadoba Pandurang and his brother Atmaram Pandurang in 1867.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prarthana Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Prarthana Samaj" ("Prayer Society") was founded in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1867 by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, along with his brother Dadoba Pandurang. (प्रार्थना समाज — 1867)

• It was a socio-religious reform movement in Maharashtra that worked for women's education, widow remarriage, the abolition of caste distinctions and the removal of child marriage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Its most famous leaders were Mahadev Govind Ranade (its guiding spirit), R. G. Bhandarkar and N. G. Chandavarkar.

• The Prarthana Samaj was strongly influenced by the Brahmo Samaj; Keshab Chandra Sen's visit to Bombay inspired its formation.

NOTE

• Key reform organisations: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Calcutta), Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839, Debendranath Tagore), Arya Samaj (1875, Swami Dayanand Saraswati, Bombay), Ramakrishna Mission (1897, Swami Vivekananda) and the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873, Jyotiba Phule).

question: What is the major function of a cell wall?
option_1: It works as a storage for material
option_2: It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
option_3: It is responsible for cell division
option_4: It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate
solution_text:
The correct answer is It provides shape and rigidity to the cell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cell wall is the tough, rigid outermost covering of plant cells (also found in fungi and bacteria). Its major function is to give the cell a definite shape, mechanical strength and rigidity, and to protect the delicate plasma membrane. (कोशिका भित्ति — आकार एवं दृढ़ता प्रदान करना)

• In plants the cell wall is made mainly of cellulose; in fungi of chitin, and in bacteria of peptidoglycan (murein).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The cell wall is freely permeable, allowing water and solutes to pass; it also enables plant cells to withstand hypotonic conditions without bursting (turgidity).

• Animal cells do not have a cell wall — they have only the plasma membrane, which is why they can change shape.

NOTE

• Functions of other organelles: vacuole — storage; nucleus/chromosomes — control of cell division and heredity; chloroplast — photosynthesis (synthesis of carbohydrate); mitochondria — the "powerhouse" producing ATP; ribosome — protein synthesis.

question: Which article of the constitution of India lays down the uniform civil code?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 44 of the Constitution states that "the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India". (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

• It is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36–51), which are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced in a court of law but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Uniform Civil Code (UCC) means one common set of personal laws (marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption) for all citizens, irrespective of religion.

• Goa has long had a common civil code (the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867); Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass a UCC Act (2024).

• The Supreme Court referred to Article 44 in the famous Shah Bano case (1985) and the Sarla Mudgal case (1995).

NOTE

• Other articles: Article 12 defines "the State" for Part III; Article 370 granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir (abrogated in August 2019); Section 377 of the IPC (not an Article) dealt with unnatural offences and was read down in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018).

question: 'In The Afternoon of Time' is an autobiographical book by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harivansh Rai Bachchan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "In the Afternoon of Time" is the English abridgement of the four-volume Hindi autobiography of the celebrated Hindi poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan, translated by Rupert Snell. (हरिवंश राय बच्चन)

• The original Hindi volumes are Kya Bhooloon Kya Yaad Karoon, Neerh Ka Nirman Phir, Basere Se Door and Dashdwar Se Sopan Tak.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Harivansh Rai Bachchan is best known for "Madhushala" (1935), a landmark work of the Chhayavaad-era Hindi poetry. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1968) and the Padma Bhushan (1976).

• He was the father of the actor Amitabh Bachchan.

NOTE

• Some autobiographies: My Years with Boss (Satyajit Ray wrote "My Years with Apu"), Dreaming Big (Sam Pitroda), Golden Girl (P. T. Usha), Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), An Autobiography / The Story of My Experiments with Truth (Jawaharlal Nehru / Mahatma Gandhi).

question: Which among the following instruments is used for measuring the humidity of the air or a gas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hygrometer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "hygrometer" is the instrument used to measure the humidity (the amount of water vapour) in the air or in a gas. (आर्द्रतामापी)

• A common type is the wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer (psychrometer), which compares readings of a dry thermometer and one with a wet wick.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bolometer" measures radiant energy / infrared radiation.

• Option 3 "Hydrometer" measures the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids — used to test battery acid and milk.

• Option 4 "Altimeter" measures altitude (height above sea level), used in aircraft.

NOTE

• Other instruments: Barometer — atmospheric pressure; Anemometer — wind speed; Seismograph — earthquake waves; Lactometer — purity of milk; Manometer — pressure of gases; Ammeter — electric current; Odometer — distance travelled by a vehicle.

question: The Family Courts (Amendment) Bill seeks to extend the application of the Family Courts Act to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Family Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced to retrospectively extend the Family Courts Act, 1984 to the states of Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland, thereby validating the family courts already functioning and the orders passed by them in these two states. (हिमाचल प्रदेश और नागालैंड)

• The Act had not been formally notified for these states, which raised doubts about the legal validity of their family courts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Family Courts Act, 1984 provides for the setting up of Family Courts to promote conciliation and speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage, divorce, maintenance, guardianship and custody of children.

• The retrospective dates in the Bill were 15 February 2019 for Himachal Pradesh and 12 September 2008 for Nagaland.

NOTE

• Family Courts are set up by State Governments in consultation with the High Courts, and are mandatory in cities with a population of over one million.

question: Saswati Sen is the proud recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2004-2005. She is recognized for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Saswati Sen is a celebrated exponent of the Kathak classical dance form and a leading disciple of the legendary Pandit Birju Maharaj of the Lucknow gharana. She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2004-2005. (कथक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh). The name comes from "Katha" (story) — the "kathakars" were storytellers who narrated epics through dance.

• Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. It is marked by intricate footwork (tatkar), fast spins (chakkars) and expressive abhinaya.

• Other Kathak greats: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan, Gopi Krishna and Kumudini Lakhia.

NOTE

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (established 1952, New Delhi) is India's national academy for music, dance and drama. The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Jim Corbett National Park is in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jim Corbett National Park is situated in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand, in the Himalayan foothills along the Ramganga river. (जिम कॉर्बेट राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — उत्तराखंड)

• Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, it is the oldest national park in India. It was renamed after the famous hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett in 1957.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was the site where Project Tiger was launched in 1973, making it India's first tiger reserve.

• Its main zones include Dhikala, Bijrani, Jhirna and Durgadevi; the park is famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger, elephants, leopards and over 600 bird species.

NOTE

• Other national parks of Uttarakhand: Nanda Devi, Valley of Flowers (both UNESCO World Heritage Sites), Rajaji, Gangotri and Govind Pashu Vihar. India's largest national park is Hemis (Ladakh).

question: ______ is used for the separation of components of a mixture containing two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distillation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Distillation" is the method used to separate two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and whose boiling points differ appreciably (generally by more than 25°C). (आसवन)

• Working principle: the mixture is heated; the liquid with the lower boiling point vaporises first, the vapour is passed through a condenser and collected separately as the distillate.

◦ Example: separating acetone (b.p. 56°C) and water (b.p. 100°C).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• If the boiling points are close, fractional distillation is used, employing a fractionating column — as in the refining of petroleum and the separation of the gases of air.

• Option 3 "Sublimation" separates a solid that changes directly into vapour (camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride, iodine) from a non-sublimable solid.

• Option 4 "Emulsification" is the mixing (not separating) of two immiscible liquids, such as oil in water.

NOTE

• Other separation techniques: filtration (insoluble solid from liquid), evaporation/crystallisation (soluble solid from solution), centrifugation (cream from milk), chromatography (dyes in ink), separating funnel (two immiscible liquids such as oil and water).

question: Late Jagjit Singh was a popular composer and a ______ singer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghazal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The late Jagjit Singh (1941–2011) was a legendary Indian ghazal singer, composer and musician, popularly called the "Ghazal King" (Ghazal Samrat). (ग़ज़ल गायक)

• He is credited with making the ghazal — a classical Urdu poetic form set to music — accessible to ordinary listeners through simple tunes and modern instrumentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was born in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, and was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2003).

• His famous albums and songs include "The Unforgettables", "Tum Itna Jo Muskura Rahe Ho", "Hothon Se Chhoo Lo Tum", "Jhuki Jhuki Si Nazar" and "Chithi Na Koi Sandesh"; he often performed with his wife Chitra Singh.

NOTE

• A ghazal is a poem of couplets (shers) sharing a common rhyme (radif/kaafiya), usually on themes of love and loss. Other noted ghazal singers: Mehdi Hassan, Ghulam Ali, Begum Akhtar, Pankaj Udhas and Talat Aziz.

question: Magha Saaji is celebrated as Makar Sankranti in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Magha Saaji" (also called Maghi Saaji or Magha Sankranti) is the name by which Makar Sankranti is celebrated in Himachal Pradesh. (हिमाचल प्रदेश — माघ साजी)

• "Saaji" is the local word derived from "Sankranti", meaning the transition of the Sun from one zodiac sign to another — here into Makar (Capricorn), in mid-January.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• People take a holy dip in rivers, distribute khichdi, ghee and chidwa (flattened rice), and sing folk songs; the festival marks the beginning of the month of Magha.

• Regional names of Makar Sankranti: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Uttarayan (Gujarat), Lohri/Maghi (Punjab), Bihu (Magh Bihu) (Assam), Poush Sankranti (West Bengal), Khichdi (Uttar Pradesh) and Makara Vilakku (Kerala — Sabarimala).

NOTE

• Makar Sankranti falls around 14–15 January every year and is one of the few Indian festivals based on the solar calendar, which is why its date is nearly fixed. It marks the beginning of Uttarayan (the sun's northward journey) and longer days.

question: Myanmar doesn't share its boundary with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sikkim does not share a boundary with Myanmar. Sikkim's international borders are with Nepal (west), China/Tibet (north and north-east) and Bhutan (east). (सिक्किम — म्यांमार से सीमा नहीं)

• Myanmar shares its border with four Indian states — Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram — with a total length of about 1,643 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India shares land borders with seven countries: Bangladesh (4,096 km — longest), China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km), Nepal (1,751 km), Myanmar (1,643 km), Bhutan (699 km) and Afghanistan (106 km — shortest).

• The Free Movement Regime (FMR) allowed people living near the India–Myanmar border to travel a short distance across without a visa.

NOTE

• States bordering China: Ladakh (UT), Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh. States bordering Nepal: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Sikkim is the only state that borders three countries — Nepal, China and Bhutan.

question: The number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period is called the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is velocity of circulation of money.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "velocity of circulation of money" is defined as the number of times a unit of money (say one rupee) changes hands during a given period of time, usually a year. (मुद्रा के संचलन का वेग)

• It is expressed in Fisher's Equation of Exchange: MV = PT, where M = money supply, V = velocity of circulation, P = price level and T = volume of transactions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "base money" (high-powered money or reserve money, M0) is the currency in circulation plus bankers' deposits with the RBI.

• Option 3 "remittances" are funds sent home by workers living abroad — India is the world's largest recipient of remittances.

• Option 4 "zero economic profit" (normal profit) is the long-run equilibrium condition of a firm under perfect competition.

NOTE

• RBI's measures of money supply: M1 (narrow money = currency with the public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI), M2, M3 (broad money = M1 + time deposits) and M4. A higher velocity of circulation, with output unchanged, tends to raise the price level.

question: Who among the following won the Meltwater Champions Chess Tour 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magnus Carlsen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Magnus Carlsen of Norway won the Meltwater Champions Chess Tour 2022, the elite online rapid chess series, retaining the title he had also won in the earlier edition. (मैग्नस कार्लसन)

• Carlsen was the reigning World Chess Champion from 2013 to 2023 and is regarded as one of the greatest players of all time, having held the record for the highest-ever Elo rating (2882).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Arjun Erigaisi and Vidit Santosh Gujrathi are leading Indian Grandmasters who took part in the Tour; Jan-Krzysztof Duda of Poland won the FIDE World Cup 2021.

• Chess is governed worldwide by FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), founded in 1924.

NOTE

• India's chess landmarks: Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Champion; Gukesh D. became the youngest World Chess Champion in 2024; the 44th Chess Olympiad was hosted by India at Mahabalipuram, Chennai (2022).

question: Who among the following Mughal emperors built Sheesh Mahal in Agra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sheesh Mahal ("Palace of Mirrors") inside the Agra Fort was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. Its walls and ceilings are inlaid with thousands of tiny mirrors that glitter in lamplight. (शीश महल — शाहजहाँ)

• It served as a royal hammam (bath) and dressing chamber for the queens.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shah Jahan (r. 1628–1658) is called the "Prince of Builders" (Engineer King). His works include the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi, the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort and the Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus).

• Agra Fort itself was built by Akbar in 1565 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Other Mughal monuments: Humayun's Tomb, Delhi (built by his widow Hamida Banu Begum — the first great Mughal garden tomb); Fatehpur Sikri, Buland Darwaza and Agra Fort (Akbar); Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb (Nur Jahan, during Jahangir's reign); Bibi ka Maqbara, Aurangabad (Aurangzeb's period).
